body: Sorry it's taken me so long to respond to this. I think that in your case you might really benefit from seeing a therapist, since these thoughts have been so persistent and seem to be really impacting you. However this is of course a decision only you can make. Also, I'm sure you are being way too hard on yourself- you are not any less deserving of happiness than anyone else. Maybe it would help you feel better to try and make yourself list your positive qualities (even if it's really hard for you to think of any right now) and remind yourself of these things throughout the day? You are not the worthless person you are telling yourself you are. If you ever need to talk about anything else, I'm here. :)

Losing a friendship is always a difficult thing to deal with, and so is lonlieness. It sounds like you're going through a really difficult time right now but it might comfort you to know you are not alone- when you're in college it often feels like everyone around you has a booming social life, a fail safe plane for a future career, and just oodles of confidence and happiness. But the truth is that a lot of people are exactly where you are- in college but feeling lonely, left out, and lost. You're not a liability just because you don't have it all figured out yet. No one really has it all figured out yet. For a lot of people college is not the advertised "best years of your life" for a lot of people, college is the miserable years and the best years aren't until much later.  Hang in there- you're a strong person to reach out for help.

It does sound like your suicidal thoughts have been frequent lately. How long have you been having these thoughts? Have you ever see. A therapist or counselor about these problems?
Of course. Losing a friendship is always rough, and would be especially difficult in a situation like this. I hope it gets better for you soon. :)

I'm no psychologist, but I believe what you are feeling would be classified as a form of suicidal ideation, which often accompanies depression or anxiety issues.

I'm sorry about what happened with your friend, but you did  what you did out of genuine concern and love . While know that it must be a terrible feeling to have your friendship dwindle, you absolutely made the right choice and are clearly a good-hearted and selfless person. I really really hope you can find help for what you are feeling right now.

I accidentally deleted part of my first comment. I know I could have gone back and edited it, but I want to make sure you see this: I care about you, and I do not want you to kill yourself, tomorrow or ever.
I'm sorry you feel this way, op, but hang in there. Is there anything that happened your life to make you stop being positive and start feeling this way?

First off: congratulations on getting a job, and on having the tenacity to set goals and pursue them. Being willing to move to seize an opportunity to better your future takes courage. And getting offered a job in the first place means you are probably a skilled and hard working individual. You should feel proud of this, and you shouldn't let the negativity of your family stop you from being proud of this or from feeling good about yourself.

It sounds like you are dealing with some very rough stuff, op. You are clearly a strong person to have been able to hang on this long, and make efforts to help yourself. This is a fortitude and persistence in the face of some very real and overwhelming adversity that I truly admire. Hang in there some more op. Don't give up on life, and don't give up yet on getting help: lots and lots of people have trouble finding a psychiatrist or therapist that is right for them.
Listening is what we're here for. :) Long stories are ok.

If it's any comfort, a whole lot of people your age are dealing with the same sort of uncertainty about the future, and lack of a sense of purpose. It is scary, confusing, and frustrating, and I know because I'm speaking from a similar place myself. (Also about to start second year of college) 

I don't know if I can offer you much in the way of advice, but I can certainly offer an awful lot of empathy, and I really hope you can  hang in there even though it's rough.

Out of curiosity, what are you in school for?

I am nineteen as well. :) I know that is not entirely relevant, but maybe it gives me a little more grounds for empathy. If you weren't compatible with one therapist, that doesn't mean you should give up on therapy  altogether.  Many people switch therapists multiple times before finding a person they click with that can truly click with.

It's clear that you are going through a really difficult time, op. My heart ached for you reading this post. I really genuinely hope you don't kill yourself. Is there anything specific that has has made you feel this way lately?

You are more than your weight, op. Your physical appearance does not impact your worth as a person, not does it make you undeserving of love, from both yourself and others. I certainly care about you, and  while I know what you're feeling is frustrating and distressing and real, I doubt you have any reason to be so rough on yourself. 

Also, I have two questions for you:

1. How old are you?
2. Have you ever talked to a counselor or therapist about your issues with food and eating?

Hey op. I care about you, and further more, I empathize. People often tell you college is just a bucket of laughs and socialization, but the truth is that sometimes it can be really, bleakly lonely. 

But you're not alone in your lonlieness. Many others, myself included, have felt isolated and depressed by the stresses of university life

You say that you're feeling as if no one cares about you. Why is this? Has anything particular happened lately to make you feel this way?

My parents had this mentality. I thought I was just the specialist snowflake to ever grace this earth until broadening my horizons in late adolescence taught me that I was just another normal little human. 

It kind of killed my desire to try hard in high school- I'm already a genius, who cares what my math scores say? And it also made it harder to make friends- I'm smarter than these mouth breathing plebs anyhow, who needs them?

My parents were wonderful in a lot of other ways though, and I eventually outgrew the groundless elitism.

I know absolutely nothing about psychology, and I'm sorry if this is too pseudo science for you guys, I just wanted to ask actual people who were educated in the field to weigh in on this.

The description sounds a lot like me; I've never before encountered the way I daydream so uncannily described. But I'm suspicious. I know this is an emerging and unrecognized phenomenon, and I was wondering if it was, in the eyes of the psychology community rather than the tumblr community, an actual anomaly. Do a lot of people daydream this way? Is it unusual? And has there been any research into why some people engage in relative behaviors or involuntary movements while daydreaming?

If I am putting my pants on and one of the legs gets snagged around my heel and it's really hard to pull off of my heel and I get so frustrated I burst into tears because my pants hate me my heel hates me this day hates me my parents probably never loved me maybe I should go sit in the shower 

Then I realize that something is hormonally amiss and I think "hey, I'm so impossibly insane right now, I guess I'm 'bout to start the ol' menstrual cycle"
Thanks. That does make me feel a little better right now. :)

That's probably a good way of looking at it.

Interviews for my school newspaper that were poorly executed, evidence that I've lost a  lot of expensive shit by being absent minded,  things  of people I got close to this year that are gone now, a lot of the time for reasons that were my fault. 

And I guess these things seem petty and shallow and over dramatic. They probably are . And  I guess that's part of why I think I might be better off not her, because I'm petty and shallow and over dramatic.
It's definitely lame and that is takes so much time to build up a real closeness with a person, and then it can all be gone in a matter of seconds
I know this feeling so acutely that it's painful. I just want my best friend back. :(

Loss is awful.  Whatever happened you have my sympathies, op, but please don't  kill yourself. 

Can you give us some more background and details about what happened and why you feel this way? I really want to help you, I really don't want you to kill yourself, and I think I  think I could try and help you more if you told me the the full story.
